name: Chennai
details: Chennai is the capital of Tamil Nadu and its main centre for business, healthcare and education. Road, rail and air links connect it to almost every part of the state, as well as to Bangalore and Pondicherry, which makes it a common starting point for one way outstation trips.
description: The capital of Tamil Nadu on the Bay of Bengal coast, known for its long beaches, old temples and busy cultural life.

name: Coimbatore
details: Coimbatore sits in the west of Tamil Nadu, close to the Nilgiri and Anamalai hills. It is a major textile and engineering centre with an airport and good road links to Ooty, Pollachi and Kerala, so it is popular for both business trips and hill-station getaways.
description: An industrial and textile centre at the foot of the Western Ghats, with a mild climate and easy access to the hills.

name: Madurai
details: Madurai is one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in India and the cultural capital of southern Tamil Nadu. The Meenakshi Amman Temple draws pilgrims and visitors all year, and the city is a convenient base for trips to Rameswaram, Kodaikanal and Kanniyakumari.
description: One of India's oldest cities, built around the Meenakshi Amman Temple and often called the Temple City.

name: Trichy
details: Tiruchirappalli, known as Trichy, lies on the Kaveri river almost in the centre of Tamil Nadu. It has an international airport, a major railway junction and the Srirangam temple island, and it links the north of the state to Madurai and the south.
description: A riverside city with a famous rock fort, large temples and some of the state's best-known colleges.

name: Pondicherry
details: Puducherry, or Pondicherry, is a Union Territory on the Coromandel coast that was a French colony until the 1950s. Its seafront, colonial quarter and nearby Auroville make it a popular weekend destination from Chennai and Bangalore.
description: A former French colony with a tree-lined seafront, colonial streets and a calm, spiritual feel.

name: Bangalore
details: Bengaluru, also called Bangalore, is the capital of Karnataka and one of India's largest technology hubs. Frequent overnight and weekend trips connect it with Chennai, Pondicherry, Vellore and Salem.
description: The capital of Karnataka and India's technology hub, known for its parks, pleasant weather and fast pace.

name: Kumbakonam
details: Kumbakonam is a temple town in the Kaveri delta, close to Thanjavur. Its many old temples, and the Mahamaham festival held once every twelve years, attract pilgrims from across India.
description: A temple town in the Kaveri delta, known for its many ancient temples and the Mahamaham festival.

name: Vellore
details: Vellore is in the north-east of Tamil Nadu, near the Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka borders. It is known for its fort and for hospitals and colleges that bring patients and students from many states, so many travellers arrive and leave by road.
description: A fort city in northern Tamil Nadu, also a major centre for medical care and education.

name: Thiruvannamalai
details: Thiruvannamalai is built around the Arunachaleswarar Temple at the foot of Arunachala hill. On every full-moon night pilgrims walk the roughly 14 km Girivalam path around the hill, and the town is busiest on those days.
description: A pilgrim town below the sacred Arunachala hill, known for its great Shiva temple and the full-moon hill walk.

name: Thanjavur
details: Thanjavur was the capital of the Chola kings and is home to the Brihadeeswara Temple, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The city is also known for Tanjore paintings, bronze work and Carnatic music.
description: The heart of the Cauvery delta and the rice bowl of Tamil Nadu, with Chola-era temples and classical arts.

name: Salem
details: Salem is an industrial city in the north-west of Tamil Nadu, known for steel, textiles and mangoes. It is the gateway to Yercaud and lies on the main road between Bangalore, Erode and Coimbatore.
description: A steel and textile city that is also the gateway to the Yercaud hills.

name: Tirunelveli
details: Tirunelveli lies on the Thamirabarani river in the far south of Tamil Nadu and is famous for its halwa. Courtallam, Papanasam and several dams are within a short drive, and Kanniyakumari is about 85 km away.
description: A southern city on the Thamirabarani river, known for the Nellaiappar Temple, nearby waterfalls and its halwa.

name: Ooty
details: Ooty, officially Udhagamandalam, is the main hill station of the Nilgiris at about 2,200 metres above sea level. The climate is cool all year, and the Nilgiri Mountain Railway, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, runs up from Mettupalayam.
description: A hill station in the Nilgiris with lakes, tea gardens and cool weather through the year.

name: Rameswaram
details: Rameswaram is an island town on the Gulf of Mannar and one of the four Char Dham pilgrimage sites. The Pamban Bridge links it to the mainland, and the road ends at Dhanushkodi on the island's eastern tip.
description: An island town and major pilgrimage centre, joined to the mainland by the Pamban Bridge.

name: Karaikudi
details: Karaikudi is the centre of Chettinad, a region known for the large mansions built by merchant families, its peppery cuisine and hand-painted Athangudi tiles.
description: The centre of the Chettinad region, known for grand mansions, spicy food and hand-made tiles.

name: Erode
details: Erode is a trading city on the Kaveri river, known for turmeric, textiles and handloom cotton. It is a major rail junction and lies between Salem and Coimbatore on the main route through western Tamil Nadu.
description: A textile and turmeric trading city on the Kaveri river.

name: Tiruppur
details: Tiruppur is India's largest hub for knitted garments and ships clothing to many countries. Business travellers make up much of the traffic, and the city is within easy reach of Coimbatore by road.
description: India's knitwear capital, known for its garment industry.

name: Kanniyakumari
details: Kanniyakumari, at the southern tip of mainland India, is where the Bay of Bengal, the Arabian Sea and the Indian Ocean meet. Visitors come for the sunrise and sunset, the Vivekananda Rock Memorial and the 133-foot Thiruvalluvar statue.
description: The southern tip of India, where three seas meet, famous for its sunrise and sunset views.

name: Kanchipuram
details: Kanchipuram is one of the seven sacred cities of India and is famous for its temples and hand-woven silk sarees. It is about 70 km from Chennai, which makes it an easy day trip.
description: A historic temple city and the home of Kanchipuram silk sarees.

name: Dindigul
details: Dindigul sits between Madurai and Coimbatore on the main highway. It is the starting point for trips to Palani, Kodaikanal and the Sirumalai hills, and it is known for its rock fort and Dindigul biryani.
description: A fort town and the gateway to the Palani and Kodaikanal hills, also known for its biryani.

name: Pollachi
details: Pollachi is a market town surrounded by coconut groves at the foot of the Anamalai hills. It is the base for Aliyar Dam, Topslip and the Anamalai Tiger Reserve, and lies about 40 km from Coimbatore.
description: A green town at the base of the Anamalai hills, surrounded by coconut farms.

name: Tenkasi
details: Tenkasi is the gateway to Courtallam, a group of waterfalls often called the Spa of South India. The falls are at their best during the monsoon months, from about June to September.
description: A town beside the Courtallam waterfalls, often called the Spa of South India.

name: Mahabalipuram
details: Mahabalipuram, also called Mamallapuram, has seventh and eighth-century Pallava monuments carved from rock, including the Shore Temple, and is listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site. It is on the East Coast Road south of Chennai.
description: A coastal town with seventh-century Pallava rock-cut monuments, listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

name: Yercaud
details: Yercaud is a small hill station in the Shevaroy hills at about 1,500 metres, not far from Salem. It is known for coffee estates, orchards and viewpoints, and stays cooler than the plains through the year.
description: A small hill station in the Shevaroy hills, with coffee plantations, lakes and viewpoints.

name: Ariyalur
details: Ariyalur sits in central Tamil Nadu and is known for limestone and cement. Its best known attraction is Gangaikonda Cholapuram, the capital built by the Chola king Rajendra Chola I, with a large Brihadisvara temple that is a UNESCO World Heritage site.
description: A district town known for its cement industry and the nearby Gangaikonda Cholapuram temple.

name: Chengalpattu
details: Chengalpattu is a district headquarters town south of Chennai on the highway to Madurai and Trichy. It is a gateway to Mahabalipuram and Kanchipuram, and has an old fort and a large lake.
description: A district headquarters on the Chennai to Madurai highway, with a historic fort.

name: Cuddalore
details: Cuddalore is a coastal district headquarters with an old port, fishing harbour and beaches, and it is well connected by road and rail with Pondicherry, Chidambaram and Chennai. Silver Beach is a popular evening spot.
description: A port town on the Bay of Bengal, south of Pondicherry.

name: Dharmapuri
details: Dharmapuri lies on NH44 between Bangalore and Salem. It is the usual base for a trip to Hogenakkal Falls on the Kaveri, where visitors take coracle rides.
description: A hilly district town on the Bangalore to Salem highway, close to Hogenakkal.

name: Kallakurichi
details: Kallakurichi is an agricultural town known for sugarcane, cashew and rice. It is the base for visiting Kalvarayan Hills and the Gomukhi dam.
description: A district town in the Villupuram belt, close to the Kalvarayan Hills.

name: Karur
details: Karur is known for home textiles, bus body building and its large number of exporters. It is on the road between Trichy, Coimbatore and Dindigul, and has several old temples.
description: A textile and bus body building hub on the Amaravathi and Kaveri rivers.

name: Krishnagiri
details: Krishnagiri sits on NH44 about 90 km from Bangalore and is known for its mangoes, its dam and its old hill fort. It is the usual last big stop before reaching Bangalore.
description: A mango growing district town on the Bangalore to Salem highway.

name: Mayiladuthurai
details: Mayiladuthurai, also called Mayavaram, is a town in the Kaveri delta with a strong Shaivite tradition and several old temples. It is a base for the Navagraha temples and for the Kaveri river bathing festival in October and November.
description: A temple town on the Kaveri delta, near Chidambaram and Kumbakonam.

name: Nagapattinam
details: Nagapattinam is an old trading port on the Bay of Bengal. Nearby is Velankanni, a major Catholic pilgrimage centre known as the Lourdes of the East, and Nagore Dargah, a famous Sufi shrine.
description: A port town on the Coromandel Coast, famous for Velankanni and Nagore Dargah.

name: Namakkal
details: Namakkal is a rocky hill town in the middle of Tamil Nadu, known for its Namakkal Fort, the 18 feet high Anjaneyar statue and its large egg and trucking industries. It is on the Salem to Karur and Trichy highways.
description: A town famous for its giant Anjaneyar statue, rock fort and the poultry and transport industry.

name: Perambalur
details: Perambalur is a small district headquarters, famous for its fossil beds at Sathanur and Ottakoil, which date back to the dinosaur era. It sits on NH38 about 55 km from Trichy.
description: A district town on the Trichy to Chennai highway.

name: Pudukkottai
details: Pudukkottai was a princely state and has an old palace, a good museum and many ancient temples. The town and its surroundings have Pallava and Chola era cave temples and the Sittanavasal Jain caves.
description: A historic town with a palace, museum and many old temples and cave shrines.

name: Ramanathapuram
details: Ramanathapuram is a coastal district headquarters with Ramalinga Vilasam Palace and long beaches. It is on the highway from Madurai to Rameswaram and is the base for visiting Dhanushkodi.
description: A coastal district town on the way to Rameswaram and Kilakarai.

name: Ranipet
details: Ranipet is a district town on the Chennai to Bangalore highway. It has a large leather and chemical industrial belt, and is close to Vellore, Arcot and Walajapet.
description: A leather and industrial town, now a district headquarters near Vellore.

name: Sivaganga
details: Sivaganga is a town in the Chettinad heartland, with an old palace, many temples and large tanks. It is a good stop between Madurai and Karaikudi.
description: The district headquarters of the Chettinad region, with palaces and temples.

name: Theni
details: Theni is a town in the Cumbum valley, surrounded by hills and farmland, and is a good base for Meghamalai, Suruli Falls and Vaigai dam. It is the gateway to Kerala at Kumily and Munnar.
description: A green farming town near the Kerala border, a base for Megamalai and Kumily.

name: Thoothukudi
details: Thoothukudi, also known as Tuticorin, is a major port, known for its salt pans, pearl fishing history and the Our Lady of Snows Basilica. It is also a good starting point for the Manapad coast and Thiruchendur.
description: A port and salt-pan town on the Gulf of Mannar, also called Pearl City.

name: Tirupathur
details: Tirupathur is a small district headquarters near Vellore and Krishnagiri and the closest town for visiting Yelagiri hill station. It lies on the Chennai to Bangalore route.
description: A town in the Jolarpettai belt, close to Yelagiri hills.

name: Tiruvallur
details: Tiruvallur is a temple town 45 km from Chennai, known for the Veeraraghava Perumal Temple, one of the 108 Divya Desams, which is believed to heal ailments. It lies on the highway to Tirupati and is close to the Pulicat Lake.
description: A district town near Chennai with the Veeraraghava Perumal Temple.

name: Tiruvarur
details: Tiruvarur is a Kaveri delta town with the large Thyagaraja Temple and its giant temple tank, and the temple car which is one of the biggest in the country. It is also the birthplace of the three great Carnatic composers.
description: A temple town and the birthplace of the Carnatic music trinity.

name: Villupuram
details: Villupuram is the junction of the Chennai, Trichy and Pondicherry rail lines and road routes. It is a convenient stop for travelling to Pondicherry, Gingee Fort and Thiruvannamalai.
description: A railway junction and district town, the gateway to Pondicherry and Gingee.

name: Virudhunagar
details: Virudhunagar is a market town known for oil, pulses and dry goods, and is on the highway between Madurai and Tirunelveli. It is also the birthplace of the leader K. Kamaraj.
description: A trading town in southern Tamil Nadu, close to Madurai, known for its oil and pulses markets.

name: Nagercoil
details: Nagercoil is a green town near the Western Ghats with coconut and banana groves. It is the best base for Kanniyakumari, Suchindram and Padmanabhapuram Palace, and has good connections to Thiruvananthapuram.
description: The main town of Kanniyakumari district, close to the southern tip of India.

name: Hosur
details: Hosur is a fast growing industrial city with a pleasant climate, near the Karnataka border and the Bangalore ring road. Many people travelling from Bangalore start their journey into Tamil Nadu from here.
description: An industrial town on the Tamil Nadu border, just 40 km from Bangalore.

name: Palani
details: Palani is one of the six abodes of Murugan and one of the most visited temples in South India. Pilgrims climb about 700 steps, or take the winch or rope car, to reach the Dandayuthapani Swami Temple on the hill.
description: A major pilgrimage town with the hill temple of Lord Murugan.

name: Kodaikanal
details: Kodaikanal lies at about 2,100 metres in the Palani hills and is one of the most visited hill stations in South India. It has a star-shaped lake, pine forests, misty viewpoints and good weather in almost every season.
description: The Princess of Hill Stations, a cool lake town in the Palani hills.

name: Valparai
details: Valparai is a high plateau of tea estates, dense forest and misty viewpoints at about 1,000 metres. The road from Pollachi has 40 hairpin bends and often shows elephants and lion-tailed macaques.
description: A quiet tea and coffee hill station on the Anamalai hills, 65 km from Pollachi.

name: Coonoor
details: Coonoor sits among tea estates on the Nilgiri hills and is known for its mild weather, Sim's Park and the toy train line that links Mettupalayam, Coonoor and Ooty. It is a popular, less crowded alternative to Ooty.
description: A cool tea-growing hill town in the Nilgiris, quieter than Ooty.

name: Kotagiri
details: Kotagiri is the oldest of the three Nilgiri hill stations and has a pleasant climate, tea gardens and viewpoints. It is a good choice for visitors who want a quieter hill station experience.
description: A calm Nilgiri hill town with tea estates, usually quieter than Ooty and Coonoor.

name: Mettupalayam
details: Mettupalayam is at the foot of the Nilgiri hills and is the starting point of the Nilgiri Mountain Railway, a UNESCO World Heritage line, and of the road up to Coonoor and Ooty. It is on the Kovai to Ooty road.
description: The foothill town where the Nilgiri toy train starts its climb to Ooty.

name: Udumalaipettai
details: Udumalaipettai is a farming town on the Coimbatore to Palani highway and the base for Amaravathi Dam, Thirumoorthy Hills and Anamalai tiger reserve. It is also on the road to Munnar.
description: A town at the foot of the Western Ghats, the road to Munnar and Amaravathi Dam.

name: Sivakasi
details: Sivakasi is a busy industrial town in Virudhunagar district, which produces most of the fireworks, safety matches and offset printing in India. It is close to Madurai and to the Srivilliputhur Andal Temple.
description: The fireworks, match and printing capital of India.

name: Rajapalayam
details: Rajapalayam is a neat, hilly town in Virudhunagar district with views of the Western Ghats. It is famous for the Rajapalayam hound dog breed, cotton yarn and sweet milk.
description: A town at the foot of the Western Ghats, known for its Rajapalayam hound dogs and cotton.

name: Kovilpatti
details: Kovilpatti is a trading town in south Tamil Nadu known for its peanut candy, which has a geographical indication tag, and for matchbox and cotton trade. It lies on the highway between Madurai and Tirunelveli.
description: A town in the Thoothukudi district, famous for kadalai mittai, a peanut candy.

name: Cumbum
details: Cumbum lies in a green valley between the Western Ghats and is known for its grape vineyards and banana plantations. It is on the route to the Kerala border at Kumily and to Thekkady.
description: A farming town in the Theni district, known for its grapes, in the Cumbum valley.

name: Chidambaram
details: Chidambaram is home to the Thillai Nataraja Temple, one of the most important Shiva temples in Tamil Nadu and the place associated with the cosmic dance of Nataraja. The town is also the seat of Annamalai University and is close to the Pichavaram mangrove forest.
description: A temple town famous for the Nataraja temple and the Annamalai University.

name: Sirkali
details: Sirkali is a Kaveri delta town with the famous Sattainathar Temple and a strong Shaivite tradition. It is close to Chidambaram, Vaitheeswaran Koil and the coast at Poompuhar.
description: A temple town known as Sattainathar Swamy temple land and for its Kaveri delta farms.

name: Arakkonam
details: Arakkonam is an important railway junction in Ranipet district and a key link between Chennai, Bangalore and Tirupati. The town also hosts INS Rajali, a major naval air station.
description: A railway junction town northwest of Chennai, with a major naval air station.

name: Ambur
details: Ambur is a busy town in north Tamil Nadu, famous for its leather industry and for Ambur biryani, a local speciality known across the state. It lies on the Chennai to Bangalore highway, which makes it an easy stop for travellers between the two cities.
description: A leather and biryani town in the Vellore district, on the Chennai to Bangalore highway.

name: Vaniyambadi
details: Vaniyambadi is a busy town on the Palar river, known for its leather industry and for biryani. It is on the road from Chennai and Vellore to Bangalore through Krishnagiri.
description: A leather town in Tirupathur district, on the Chennai to Bangalore highway.

name: Gudiyatham
details: Gudiyatham lies on the Palar river valley between Vellore and Vaniyambadi. It is close to the Gudiyatham hills and to the Mordhana dam, and sits on the Chennai to Bangalore highway belt.
description: A town on the Vellore to Krishnagiri route, known for beedi and handloom work.

name: Tindivanam
details: Tindivanam sits where the roads to Pondicherry, Gingee and Thiruvannamalai meet on NH32. It is a convenient stop between Chennai and the southern towns.
description: A town on the Chennai to Pondicherry and Villupuram road, with a famous Gingee link.

name: Gingee
details: Gingee, near Villupuram, is known for its Gingee Fort, which spreads over three hills and was once called the Troy of the East. The fort is a favourite of history lovers and is well worth a half day.
description: A town with the famous Gingee fort, one of the most impressive hill forts in India.

name: Neyveli
details: Neyveli is a township in Cuddalore district with one of the biggest lignite mining operations in India. The town is neat and green, with wide roads and parks, and is close to Chidambaram and Villupuram.
description: A planned township built around a large lignite mine and power plants.

name: Attur
details: Attur lies in the Vashishta river valley between Salem and Villupuram. It is known for agriculture and for its old fort, and it is the usual stop for visitors heading to the Kalrayan Hills and Yercaud.
description: A town in the Salem district in the Salem to Villupuram corridor, close to the Kalrayan Hills.

name: Mettur
details: Mettur is home to the Stanley Reservoir, one of the largest dams in India, built across the Kaveri in 1934. The dam park, power station and the hills of the Shervarayan range around make for a pleasant day trip from Salem.
description: A town best known for the Mettur Dam on the Kaveri.

name: Tiruchengode
details: Tiruchengode is a town in Namakkal district known for the Ardhanareeswarar Temple on a rocky hill, with a long flight of steps up to the shrine. It is also well known for rigs and tankers and for the textile industry.
description: A hill temple town known for its Ardhanareeswarar temple and its lorry body building.

name: Rasipuram
details: Rasipuram lies at the foot of the Kolli Hills and is a stop for visitors heading to Kolli Hills, Namakkal and Salem. It is also a centre for textile weaving and agricultural trade.
description: A town in the Namakkal district, known for Kolli Hills access and Kasi Viswanathar temple.

name: Bhavani
details: Bhavani is on the banks of the Kaveri, at its confluence with the Bhavani river and the mythical Amudha river, called Koodudhurai. It is known for the Sangameswarar Temple and for its hand-woven carpets and jamakkalam bed covers.
description: A temple town at the meeting point of the Kaveri and Bhavani rivers, near Erode.

name: Gobichettipalayam
details: Gobichettipalayam, often called Gobi, is a green town known for coconut, banana and sugarcane farming along the Lower Bhavani canal. It is also a favourite location for Tamil films.
description: A prosperous farming town in the Erode district, often used for film shoots.

name: Sathyamangalam
details: Sathyamangalam lies on the Bhavani river and is close to a large tiger reserve and elephant corridor. It is on the route between Erode, Mysore and Ooty through the Dimbam ghat road.
description: A forest town at the foot of the Nilgiris, near the Sathyamangalam tiger reserve.

name: Perundurai
details: Perundurai is on the Erode to Coimbatore road and has a large SIPCOT industrial estate. It is also a hub for coconut and turmeric farming.
description: A town in Erode district, known for its industrial estate and medical college.

name: Dharapuram
details: Dharapuram is an agricultural and trading town known for its textiles and for being close to the Amaravathi river. It is on the way between Coimbatore, Palani and Karur.
description: A trading town in the Tiruppur district on the bank of the Amaravathi river.

name: Palladam
details: Palladam is a busy power loom and poultry town on the Coimbatore to Tiruppur road, with fast links to Coimbatore airport. It is well placed for travellers heading between Coimbatore, Tiruppur and Pollachi.
description: A textile and power loom town between Coimbatore and Tiruppur.

name: Avinashi
details: Avinashi is a busy town in Tiruppur district on the Coimbatore to Salem highway, close to the Tiruppur knitwear hub. It is best known for the Avinashilingeswarar Temple, one of the old Kongu Nadu Shiva temples, whose temple car festival draws large crowds each year.
description: A temple and textile town near Tiruppur, known for the ancient Avinashiappar temple.

name: Sriperumbudur
details: Sriperumbudur is an industrial hub on the Chennai to Bangalore highway, with large car and electronics plants. It is also the birthplace of the saint Ramanujacharya, with an important temple dedicated to him.
description: A town near Chennai with the birthplace of Ramanuja and a large industrial belt.

name: Tambaram
details: Tambaram is a busy suburb of Chennai and an important railway junction on the Chennai to Chengalpattu line. It is home to an air force station, Madras Christian College and many other institutions.
description: A major suburb in south Chennai with a large air force station and many colleges.

name: Avadi
details: Avadi is part of the Chennai metropolitan area and is home to defence factories, a heavy vehicles factory and an air force station. It has good road and suburban rail links to central Chennai and to the airport.
description: A large industrial and defence suburb in the north-west of Chennai.

name: Thiruchendur
details: Thiruchendur is a coastal town in Thoothukudi district and home to the Subramaniya Swamy Temple, one of the six abodes of Murugan, located right on the seashore. It is an important pilgrimage centre and a short drive from Tirunelveli.
description: A seashore temple town with one of the six abodes of Lord Murugan.

name: Courtallam
details: Courtallam is a small town near Tenkasi known for its many waterfalls on the Chittar river. The falls are especially strong during the season from June to September, and are believed to have healing properties.
description: A waterfall town in the Western Ghats, often called the Spa of South India.

name: Karaikal
details: Karaikal is one of the four regions of Puducherry and has a calm beach, French style buildings and the Thirunallar Dharbaranyeswarar Temple, famous for Saturn worship. It is well connected with Nagapattinam, Kumbakonam and Thanjavur.
description: A coastal town in the Puducherry union territory, with a French colonial past.

name: Auroville
details: Auroville is an experimental township founded in 1968, just north of Pondicherry. People from many countries live and work here, and visitors come for the Matrimandir, a large golden sphere used for silent meditation, and for the craft and organic food outlets.
description: An international township near Pondicherry, built around the golden Matrimandir.
